title: Cadet band, bugle and first cornet
summary: He starts on drums in a boys' cadet band under Colonel Hughes and Professor Blue, moves to bugle, then gets a cornet in 1911 before an encampment trip.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: Well the first music I heard was what they had a Cudded Band called the Nice Epiphance Cudded Band. And I started playing in that band as a drummer. That was back in 1906. Did you have any lessons on drums? Did you just pick it up? No, see it was at that time they called it the Nice Epiphance Cadets. It's the same at the present time you'd have the Boy Scouts. Oh yes, yes. You know, but just the kids in the neighborhood. They used to all, and this nice epiphance was an organization that took all the kids off the street so they had some place to go. And they had a man by the name of Colonel Hughes we called him. And he took us and learned us how to drill, regular formation drill, and he organized the band. First he joined us at the trumpet and bugle horn. And of course I was playing drums then. Yes. We had a leader by the name of Blue, Professor Blue, who was the trumpet player. But he had lost his lip, his lip had split straight down and he couldn't play no more. But he was interested in children. So he said he was a trainer. For some reason or another he liked me and he put me off the drums and gave me a bugle. Oh yes. But he was leading up to the trumpet.

You learned that when you were just a boy too, very often. That's right. And I was, when I was around seven years old, that's when I got on this bugle. It was like that. And he kept me on this bugle about a year. Well, it was longer than that. Because we went to the end of the, because at that time the KP used to go away every two years, what they called an encampment. It used to take the boys to band with them. Yes. And we went to In and Out with Indiana in 1911. In 1911. And that was just before we went there was when he put the trumpet in my hand. But he had learned me, the fingering, from the bugle and everything. And he told me to start to, told me to start to play. That was 1911. When did you get your first, did you get a cornet or a trumpet first? No, I got a cornet, regular cornet, a con cornet. Yep. Con cornet. And then for that.
That's right. And then for that my mother bought me a one. Be sure, be sure. Be sure. Be sure. Be sure. That was 1911.
